tasks.short: Help transition photonic prototypes into production.

steps.what: Review actual photonic prototype requirements, test evidence and production constraints
Write and check actual optical alignment, assembly and test transfer instructions
Save the final transfer instructions in the production-accessible document record
Support actual photonic assembly trials, alignment and production test setup
Resolve actual prototype-to-production issues with manufacturing colleagues
Record and check actual transfer findings and resulting instruction revisions
outputs: checked final transfer outcome and revision record

steps.what: Save the actual transfer outcome and instruction revisions

tasks.design: Configure native {DOCS} photonic transfer-instruction fields and evidence references. Keep actual assembly/alignment trials and manufacturing troubleshooting human, and record actual outcomes and instruction revisions only after the trial.

tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and controlled revision links.
tasks.still_hard: Alignment sensitivity and different production capabilities.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve actual photonic behaviour during production transfer.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated instruction preparation; production-transfer responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native transfer-document fields reduce repeated references without conducting photonic production trials or solving alignment issues.

assumptions: Boundary is engineer transition assistance and own transfer records. Design/test owners supply actual revision, parts, optical requirements, alignment method and test evidence; production owner actual constraints. Engineer verifies context in s1, selects and writes instructions in s2 and captures actual trial outcomes in s6. Missing evidence manually resolved, no free manufacturing recipe or presumed successful transfer.

tasks.short: Write photonics research reports and project proposals.

steps.what: Verify actual photonics research evidence, project constraints and report or proposal purpose
Choose supported findings or proposed research activities, assumptions and resource needs
Populate selected optical plots, result tables or proposal resource tables
Write report or proposal narrative from actual evidence and selected content

loop.purpose: Compose selected photonics findings or proposal
loop.input: verified evidence and engineer selected document content
loop.output: draft prose with source references and explicit assumptions
loop.check: Engineer checks optical meaning, result versus proposed activity, units, budget scope, omitted failures and unsupported commitments
loop.stop: Missing evidence or costs, changed scope or two failed revisions requires manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Native tables/headings first; variable technical explanations need bounded prose

steps.what: Check complete final photonics document against evidence and chosen scope
outputs: checked final photonics report or proposal

steps.what: Save the final photonics report or proposal
inputs: checked final photonics report or proposal

tasks.design: Configure native {OTHER}/{DOCS} result and resource-table links first, then bounded prose drafting. Engineer selects technical content and checks the complete final document before save; writing a proposal does not submit it or authorise expenditure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked outputs and source-grounded drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Defensible optical claims and credible proposed research.
tasks.human_edge: Choose conclusions or project scope that actual evidence supports.
tasks.altitude: Less writing preparation; project and scientific judgement unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native report links and bounded technical drafting can reduce photonics writing preparation without selecting research conclusions or funding commitments.

assumptions: Boundary is writing through actual document save. Test owners supply actual optical variables, values, units, configuration and source references; project/cost owners actual scope and resource estimates where a proposal requires them. Engineer verifies sources in s1 and selects content and actual figures in s2. Missing evidence or costs requires manual resolution, not invented results.
